added_models.model: Human platelet aggregometry and humanized-mouse thrombus formation (acalabrutinib vs ibrutinib)

safety.note: Light-transmission aggregometry on healthy-volunteer and CLL-patient platelets, plus a humanized VWF mouse thrombus model, predicted acalabrutinib impairs platelets less than ibrutinib.
safety.short: Platelet assays predict less bleeding than ibrutinib
safety.quote: acalabrutinib appears to have fewer effects than ibrutinib on platelets in aggregometry assays and in a humanized mouse model of thrombus formation.
safety.confidence_note: Quote verbatim in the bundled review text (pharmacology section, study report r2017005). The single-arm MCL data in the same review (hemorrhage 31.5%) has no ibrutinib comparator, so it cannot test a relative prediction.
safety.judgement: The prediction is relative (fewer platelet effects than ibrutinib, a sibling outside the member list), so it opens untested until a head-to-head trial; first use proxied by the review date.

safety.note: In the head-to-head CLL trial acalabrutinib had fewer bleeding events than ibrutinib (38.0% vs 51.3%), as the platelet assays predicted; major bleeding was similar.
safety.short: Fewer bleeds than ibrutinib, as predicted
safety.quote: Bleeding events were less frequent with acalabrutinib (n = 101 [38.0%]) versus ibrutinib (n = 135 [51.3%]; Data Supplement).
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC8547923). Major bleeding comparable (4.5% vs 5.3%), so agreement is on any-grade bleeding only. Imported from CLL; no RA comparison of the platelet prediction exists.
safety.judgement: Paired comparison: the trial does not cite the platelet assays, so comparison_stated false with the FDA review as model side. Scored same with source_calls_it partial because major bleeding did not differ. On-target harm, single modality, imported_from CLL per the safety transfer rule.
safety.magnitude_basis: any-grade bleeding incidence, acalabrutinib vs ibrutinib
safety.population: Previously treated CLL with del(17p) or del(11q) (imported)

considered_not_added: Dog 91-day toxicology platelet aggregation (acalabrutinib, FDA NDA 210259: 'Unremarkable') vs 31.5% hemorrhage in MCL: not added; whether dog platelets can show BTK-dependent GPVI dysfunction (the species-capability test for a silent model) is unresolved, and the checker raised it as a rule question. Agonist used in the dog assay is not stated in the review.

Fenebrutinib population PK, exposure-response and model-based meta-analysis (Chan 2020, Pharm Res, doi 10.1007/s11095-019-2752-y): built on the Phase 2 RA data itself, an analysis of patient data rather than a model system with a prior prediction.
Evobrutinib mouse CIA/SLE PK/PD model (Haselmayer 2019 J Immunol, 80% blood BTK occupancy linked to near-complete disease inhibition): same system as the draft's cia-occupancy-pkpd dose track.
Fenebrutinib healthy-volunteer PK/PD simulation (Herman 2018 CPT): human data, same occupancy/inhibition exposure target already tracked; no in-vitro-vs-in-vivo comparison stated in the abstract.
X-linked agammaglobulinemia (human BTK loss of function) as a genetic model for RA: no source comparing it with BTK-inhibitor RA trial results found.
Patient-derived RA synovial tissue / ex vivo patient cells with member BTK inhibitors: no study linking ex vivo response to trial or patient response found.
QSP model of BTK-inhibitor occupancy in B-cell malignancies (2025, CPT:PSP doi 10.1002/psp4.13307): built after occupancy data were known, in oncology, and engagement occupancy is already tracked.

Ex vivo CLL/MCL patient platelet study showing class-wide aggregation impairment regardless of selectivity (2025, J Clin Exp Hematop doi 10.3960/jslrt.25028): model-side data only, no new patient-outcome comparison; not read beyond title.

gaps.lead: Safety, imported from MCL: acalabrutinib 91-day dog platelet aggregation 'Unremarkable' (FDA NDA 210259) vs 31.5% MCL hemorrhage
gaps.detail: Silent-model rule needs the species able to show BTK-dependent GPVI platelet dysfunction; dog capability unresolved (checker rule question) and agonist unstated; acalabrutinib platelet safety is tracked by human-platelet-aggregometry-acala-vs-ibru (safety 2-3).

gaps.lead: Efficacy patient_trials: NCT02387762 (acalabrutinib + MTX) registered primary DAS28-CRP week 4, results 2019-03-26
gaps.detail: Covered: check.json efficacy 2 note already flags NCT02387762 DAS28-CRP wk4 as the registered primary (posted 2019-03-26), and the lead only relabels a patient_trials item; efficacy 2 stays contra, year 2019 (BMS-986142 registry 2019-05-28).

gaps.lead: Efficacy/dose: spebrutinib NCT01975610 primary ACR20 week 4 missed (P=0.25, epub 2019-11-13) at 83% median BTK occupancy
gaps.detail: Covered: check.json dose 3 note raises spebrutinib and its adjudication (rule v4) scores dose on its own prediction, so a target-reached failure is same, not a 2019 contra. Re-opened Schafer 2019 (PMC7021855, epub 2019-11-13): 375 mg/day gave median BTK occupancy 83% but the paper ties the dose to no CIA-derived occupancy target, so no stated dose prediction to score; the efficacy miss (P=0.25) is already in efficacy 2 patient_trials, after the 2019-05-28 contra, so no status or year changes.
